analysis.title: Markets On The Move - APAC Equity Flows Sell Skewed; Locals Pay USDCNH Points
key_insights: Taiwan flows are 72% sellers as TAIEX fell on a knee-jerk reaction after Intel slumped 23% on results that missed expectations, losing 46K and the 6-month moving average at 45314.
Tech/AI was hit hardest in Taiwan, with limit-down moves in Delta (2308) and Chroma (2360).
Korea's KOSPI fell more than 5%. Foreign investors sold $675 mn and local institutions $297 mn of tech amid anxiety about AI cash burn into month-end. Breadth is 7:1 decliners.
Hong Kong/China flows are 53% to sell, including 5% in shorts. The desk is selling energy, tech and industrials and buying banks, insurance and healthcare.
Japan flows are net flat. Buying in defensives, railways and shippers is offset by selling in technology and consumer staples.
ASEAN flows are 63% better to sell, most active in Thailand. Industrials face selling in the Philippines and Singapore, while utilities draw inflows in Thailand, the Philippines and Singapore.
Australia flows are 59% sell skewed, concentrated in telecoms, while the desk is buying financials and industrials.
India shows an active buy skew on the UBS pad, driven by inflows in telecoms, IT, industrials and financials, with two-way interest in banks.
USDCNH eased to 6.6550 as dollar rates moved lower overnight. The USDCNY fix was lowered from 6.7147 to 6.7138, and its beta to the basket remains low at around 20%.
USDCNH forward points rebounded and implied yields edged lower. The desk saw profit-taking interest alongside paying interest from local names.

market_movers.rationale: Intel slumped 23% after results missed expectations, triggering a sell-off in Taiwan tech and AI names.

sector_views.rationale: Heavy selling in Taiwan, Korea and Japan tech. The desk is selling Taiwan semiconductor bluechips and networking, while buying mature foundry and server rail kit.
The desk is buying banks and insurance in Hong Kong/China and financials in Australia. India shows inflows in financials.
The Hong Kong/China desk is buying healthcare.
The Hong Kong/China desk is selling energy.
Utilities are drawing inflows in Thailand, the Philippines and Singapore.

earnings_insights: Intel results missed expectations (reported, per the desk) and the stock slumped 23%. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
risk_factors: Investor anxiety around AI cash burn into month-end, cited as the driver of the Korea tech sell-down.
Spillover from the Intel earnings miss into Asian tech and AI supply chains.
vol_and_positioning: Hong Kong/China flows are 53% to sell, including 5% in shorts.
Taiwan flows are 72% sellers, ASEAN 63% better to sell, Australia 59% sell skewed.
USDCNH forward points rebounded while implied yields edged lower, with profit-taking and local paying interest.
